synopsis: The booklet reports that China's Coal Mine Safety Regulations require underground trackless rubber-tired vehicles moving in the same direction to maintain at least 50 m separation, citing a July 2023 article in Meikuang Anquan rather than a review of the regulatory text [f2298, f2299, f15591]. It identifies this distance as the nearest off-road relative of its on-road headway test distances and recommends configurable collision mitigation that can meet China's following-distance expectation [f13890, f15597]. A dedicated, verified Chinese national automatic-braking acceptance rule was not found, and Chinese GB or GB/T adoptions of ISO 21815, ISO 16001, ISO 17757 and ISO 19014 were not established; these are evidence gaps, not proof that relevant standards do not exist [f2300, f15592]. Likewise, the absence finding for ML-based off-road collision-avoidance rules does not establish an absence of AI legislation in China [f2394]. Separately, China conditionally approved Synopsys's acquisition of Ansys with stipulations on customer contracts [f8879].
